flows.name: Discover TidyDash on the landing page
flows.goal: Understand what TidyDash is for and start toward an account.

steps.userAction: The visitor opens the landing page.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows what TidyDash personal dashboards are for, how creating a dashboard and adding note, counter, checklist and link-list widgets works, and ways to sign up or sign in.

steps.userAction: The visitor chooses to sign up or sign in.
steps.websiteResponse: The website directs the visitor to sign up or sign in to start.

flows.outcome: Nothing is saved; the visitor knows how to start and is directed to sign up or sign in.

flows.name: Sign up as a member
flows.goal: Create an account to own private dashboards.

steps.userAction: The visitor chooses to sign up.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows an empty account credentials form with a way to submit or go back.

steps.userAction: The visitor fills in the account credentials and submits.
steps.websiteResponse: The website creates the account, signs the member in and shows their empty dashboard space ready to create a dashboard.

alternatives.condition: The email is missing or badly formed, or the password is shorter than 8 characters.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website marks the fields and keeps what was typed.
The website keeps the values and offers to retry.

alternatives.condition: The email already has an account.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website says an account with that email already exists and offers to sign in instead, keeping what was typed.
Nothing is saved; the website shows the landing page as it was.

flows.outcome: Account created and member signed in; refresh still shows them signed in with an empty dashboard list.

flows.name: Sign in as a member
flows.goal: Sign back in to access my dashboards.

steps.userAction: The returning member chooses to sign in.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows an empty account credentials form with a way to submit or go back.

steps.userAction: The member fills in the account credentials and submits.
steps.websiteResponse: The website verifies the member and shows only their own dashboards with name and last-edited time ordered most-recently-edited first, with ways to create or open one.

alternatives.condition: The email is missing or badly formed, or the password is missing.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website marks the fields and keeps what was typed.
The website keeps the values and offers to retry.

alternatives.condition: The email and password do not match.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website says the email and password do not match, keeps the email and offers to try again.

alternatives.condition: The member has no dashboards yet.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website shows an empty dashboard space with a way to create a new dashboard.
Nothing is saved; the website shows the landing page as it was.

flows.outcome: Member signed in; refresh still shows them signed in with their own dashboards.

flows.name: Sign out
flows.goal: End the session on this device.

steps.userAction: The member chooses to sign out.
steps.websiteResponse: The website ends the session, hides private dashboards and shows the public landing page with ways to sign up or sign in.

flows.outcome: Member signed out and private data hidden; refresh still shows signed-out state.

flows.name: Create a new dashboard
flows.goal: Start a new empty dashboard in the editor.

steps.userAction: The member opens their dashboard space.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows only their own dashboards with name and last-edited time ordered most-recently-edited first and a way to create a new dashboard.

steps.userAction: The member chooses to create a new dashboard.
steps.websiteResponse: The website creates an empty dashboard with a default name, saves it automatically with the current last-edited time and opens it in the editor.

alternatives.condition: The member has no dashboards yet.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website shows an empty dashboard space with a way to create a new dashboard.
The website keeps the list as it was and offers to retry.

flows.outcome: New empty dashboard saved with default name and current last-edited time; it appears first in the list and is still there after a refresh, open in the editor.

flows.name: View my dashboard list
flows.goal: See all my dashboards and pick one to open.

steps.userAction: The member opens their dashboard space.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows only their own dashboards with each name and when it was last edited ordered most-recently-edited first, with ways to create a new dashboard or open one.

alternatives.condition: The member has no dashboards yet.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website shows an empty dashboard space with a way to create a new dashboard.

flows.outcome: Nothing changes; refresh still shows the same private list ordered most-recently-edited first.

flows.name: Rename a dashboard

steps.userAction: The member chooses to rename a dashboard.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the current dashboard name ready to edit.

steps.userAction: The member edits the dashboard name and confirms.
steps.websiteResponse: The website saves the new name automatically, updates the last-edited time and shows the renamed dashboard in place.

alternatives.condition: The name is longer than 100 characters.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website marks the field and keeps what was typed.
The website keeps the values and offers to retry.
The website shows that the dashboard is gone and shows the updated list.
Nothing is saved; the website shows the dashboard as it was.
The website shows that the dashboard is gone and shows the updated list.

flows.outcome: Dashboard name updated and saved with new last-edited time; still renamed after a refresh.

flows.name: Duplicate a dashboard
flows.goal: Make a full copy of a dashboard including its widgets.

steps.userAction: The member opens their dashboard space.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows only their own dashboards with name and last-edited time and a way to duplicate a dashboard.

steps.userAction: The member chooses to duplicate a dashboard.
steps.websiteResponse: The website creates a full copy including all widgets and their content named like Copy of the original, saves it and shows it in the list.

alternatives.condition: The member has no dashboards yet.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website shows an empty dashboard space with a way to create a new dashboard.
The website keeps the list as it was and offers to retry.
The website shows that the dashboard is gone and shows the updated list.

flows.outcome: Copy saved with all widgets and content; both original and copy are still there after a refresh.

flows.name: Delete a dashboard
flows.goal: Permanently remove a dashboard and its widgets.

steps.userAction: The member views the dashboard list.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows only the member's own dashboards with each name and when it was last edited, ordered most-recently-edited first, each with a way to delete it.
The website permanently removes the dashboard and its widgets and shows the updated dashboard list.

alternatives.websiteResponse: The website shows that there are no dashboards yet and offers a way to create a new dashboard.
The website keeps the dashboard and offers to retry.
Nothing is deleted; the website shows the dashboard list as it was.

flows.outcome: Dashboard and its widgets removed; still gone after a refresh and list no longer shows it.

flows.name: Add a widget to a dashboard
flows.goal: Add a new widget of a chosen type to the dashboard.
preconditions: A dashboard is open in the editor.

steps.userAction: The member views the open dashboard in the editor.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the dashboard name and its widgets in their saved order, with a way to add a widget of each type.

steps.userAction: The member chooses a widget type and adds the widget.
steps.websiteResponse: The website appends a new widget with default title and medium size, saves it automatically, updates the dashboard last-edited time and shows it in order.

alternatives.websiteResponse: The website shows that the dashboard is empty and offers a way to add a widget.
The website marks the type choice and keeps the editor as it was.
The website keeps the chosen type and offers to retry.
The website shows that the dashboard is gone and shows the dashboard list.

flows.outcome: New widget saved with defaults and appended in order; still there after a refresh with updated last-edited time.

flows.name: Configure and use widget content
flows.goal: Fill in and use the content of my widgets.
preconditions: A dashboard with at least one widget is open in the editor.

steps.userAction: The member views the widgets in the open dashboard.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows each widget with its title, type-specific content and size in saved order, ready to edit and use.

steps.userAction: The member types note text in a note widget.
steps.websiteResponse: The website saves the note text automatically, updates the dashboard last-edited time and shows the updated note.

steps.userAction: The member edits the counter label and number.
steps.websiteResponse: The website saves the label and number automatically, updates the dashboard last-edited time and shows the updated counter.

steps.userAction: The member increases or decreases a counter.
steps.websiteResponse: The website changes the number by 1 per use, saves it automatically, updates the dashboard last-edited time and shows the new number.

steps.userAction: The member adds, edits, ticks, unticks or removes checklist items.
steps.websiteResponse: The website saves each checklist change automatically, keeps ticked items visible, updates the dashboard last-edited time and shows the updated checklist.

steps.userAction: The member adds, edits or removes link titles and addresses and selects a link to open it.
steps.websiteResponse: The website saves each link change automatically, updates the dashboard last-edited time, shows the updated link list and opens a selected link in a new browser tab.

alternatives.websiteResponse: The website shows that the dashboard has no widgets yet and offers a way to add a widget.

alternatives.condition: The note text is longer than allowed.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website marks the note text and keeps what was typed.
The website keeps the typed text and offers to retry.

alternatives.condition: The counter number is not a whole number.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website marks the counter number and keeps what was typed.
The website keeps the typed values and offers to retry.
The website keeps the previous number and offers to retry.

alternatives.condition: A new checklist item has no text.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website marks the item text and keeps what was typed.
The website keeps the typed values and offers to retry.

alternatives.condition: The link address is missing or is not a valid web address.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website marks the link address and keeps what was typed.
The website keeps the typed values and offers to retry.

alternatives.condition: The dashboard or widget is already gone.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website shows that the dashboard is gone and shows the dashboard list.

flows.outcome: Widget content saved automatically; still there after a refresh and dashboard shows updated last-edited time.

flows.name: Manage widgets
flows.goal: Arrange, resize, rename and remove widgets.
preconditions: A dashboard with at least one widget is open in the editor.

steps.userAction: The member views the widgets in the open dashboard.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows each widget with its title and size in saved order, each with ways to rename, move, resize and remove it.

steps.userAction: The member renames a widget.
steps.websiteResponse: The website saves the new title automatically, updates the dashboard last-edited time and shows the renamed widget in place.

steps.userAction: The member moves a widget to a new position relative to the other widgets.
steps.websiteResponse: The website saves the new order automatically, updates the dashboard last-edited time and shows the widgets in the new order.

steps.userAction: The member changes a widget size between small, medium and large.
steps.websiteResponse: The website saves the new size automatically, updates the dashboard last-edited time and shows the widget in the new size.
The website removes the widget immediately, updates the dashboard last-edited time and shows the remaining widgets in order.

alternatives.websiteResponse: The website shows that the dashboard has no widgets yet and offers a way to add a widget.

alternatives.condition: The widget title is longer than allowed.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website marks the title and keeps what was typed.
The website keeps the typed title and offers to retry.
The website keeps the previous order and offers to retry.

alternatives.condition: The size choice is missing or not recognized.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website marks the size choice and keeps the widget as it was.
The website keeps the chosen size and offers to retry.
The website keeps the widget and offers to retry.

alternatives.condition: The dashboard or widget is already gone.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website shows that the dashboard is gone and shows the dashboard list.
Nothing is removed; the website shows the widgets as they were.

flows.outcome: Renames, order, sizes saved and removals gone; refresh still shows the same arrangement with updated last-edited time.

flows.name: Open a dashboard in the editor
flows.goal: Open one of my existing dashboards to view and edit its widgets.

steps.userAction: The member views the dashboard list.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows only the member's own dashboards with each name and when it was last edited, ordered most-recently-edited first, with a way to open one.

steps.userAction: The member chooses a dashboard to open.
steps.websiteResponse: The website opens the chosen dashboard in the editor showing its name and widgets in saved order, ready to add, configure and manage widgets.

alternatives.websiteResponse: The website shows that there are no dashboards yet and offers a way to create a new dashboard.

alternatives.condition: The chosen dashboard is already gone.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website shows that the dashboard is gone and shows the updated dashboard list.
The website keeps the dashboard list and offers to retry.

alternatives.condition: The dashboard has no widgets yet.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website shows that the dashboard is empty and offers a way to add a widget.

flows.outcome: The chosen dashboard is open in the editor showing its widgets; it is still open in the editor after a refresh.

fields.label: Email
fields.meaning: The member's sign-in address for their private dashboards

fields.label: Password
fields.meaning: Secret that proves ownership of the account

fields.label: Dashboard name
fields.meaning: How the member refers to the dashboard in the list and editor

fields.label: Widget title
fields.meaning: Heading shown on the widget to say what it is for

fields.label: Widget type
fields.meaning: What kind of content the widget holds

fields.label: Widget size
fields.meaning: How large the widget appears relative to other widgets

fields.label: Note text
fields.meaning: Plain text kept in a note widget
fields.example: Call the dentist on Tuesday about the checkup.

fields.label: Counter label
fields.meaning: What the counter number is counting

fields.label: Checklist item text
fields.meaning: One task line inside a checklist widget

fields.label: Link title
fields.meaning: Readable name shown for a saved web address

fields.label: Link address
fields.meaning: Web address opened when the link is selected

fields.label: Counter value
fields.meaning: Current number kept in a counter widget

fields.label: Checklist item done
fields.meaning: Whether a checklist item is ticked off

steps.userAction: The member chooses to delete the item.
steps.websiteResponse: The website asks the member to confirm that deletion is permanent or to cancel.

steps.userAction: The member confirms permanent deletion.
steps.websiteResponse: The website records the confirmation to proceed with permanent deletion.

alternatives.websiteResponse: Nothing is deleted; the website shows the content as it was.
The website keeps the item and offers to retry.
The website shows that the item is already gone and shows the updated list.

assumptions.text: Removing a widget asks for confirmation first and then deletes immediately with no trash or undo, reading A09's immediately as no restore after confirm.
Renaming, duplicating, resizing, repositioning and editing any widget content all count as dashboard changes that trigger autosave and update the dashboard last-edited time.
